Tower House School
Tower House School
Learning is life's greatest adventure and at Tower House School we want every boy to arrive each day with a sense of joy, excitement and wonder at what lies ahead.
School should be fun and our innovative and creative curriculum, relaxed and happy ethos and excellent teachers offer just that, in and beyond the classroom. We want our boys to find what they love and to feel inspired to explore those areas with open hearts and minds. This can happen because of our strong commitment to each individual and the school's uniquely supportive environment, in which all boys feel valued and able to contribute on a daily basis.
What makes Tower House Special?
Small & Personal
Limited class sizes and single form entry leads to a unique, nurturing and incredibly friendly environment where every boy is valued and the whole community knows and supports each other.
Individual Focus
We understand boys and pride ourselves on finding an Opportunity for Every Boy. With significant specialist teaching from a young age no child gets left behind in or out of the classroom and we are totally committed to supporting each boy to achieve their best, nurture their character and celebrate where their passions lie.
Truly Independent
As a not-for-profit Charitable Trust, we are excellent value and are able to make every decision for the benefit of the boys in the school; an increasingly rare privilege.
Strong Links to OVS
We are proud that our close collaboration with the Old Vicarage School in Richmond enables our boys to work and socialise with girls as they grow up, leading to a healthy understanding of how positive and happy relationships are formed, whilst also ensuring that our boys are challenged with different perspectives and views of the world. Tower House and Old Vicarage are close friends sharing the best of both worlds for our pupils and their families.

We are proud of the breadth and depth of our scholarships, with over half of this year’s cohort of Year 8 boys awarded scholarships across different aspects of school life – academics, music, art, sports and drama.
6 Location
Situated 6 miles from Central London on the edge of Richmond Park, THS has access to excellent public transport links into Waterloo and Clapham Junction.
200Facilities
With seating for 200, the new Evans Hall is a fantastic space for drama productions, assemblies, sport and clubs.
80%Music
Over 80% of pupils learn an instrument at THS, and we are proud that 17 different instruments are taught by specialist music staff. This breadth and depth enables 13 ensembles, including a full Orchestra, Swing Band, Brass Ensemble, Saxophone and Clarinet Ensemble, String Quartet, Woodwind Band and two Rock Bands! Our Senior Choir is also very proud to have been awarded silver in the 2026 UK Schools Music Festival.
2Transport
Two daily bus routes from Barnes and Putney are available each morning to help our families with transport to school.
40ICT
As well as a fully equipped ICT suite, THS also has 40 laptops and tablets available for use in the Junior and Senior School classrooms.
100%Sport
All boys from Year 3 to Year 8 are given frequent opportunities to represent THS in competitive matches against local schools.

THS are the proud winners of the 2023 Talk Education Award for Innovation in Education in Creative and Performing Arts. We are also the Finalists for the 2023 Independent School of the Year Award in Performing Arts.

The History of Tower House
1931
The Sheen School Of Music
Prior to being founded in 1931, Tower House was known as The Sheen School of Music. The original building on Sheen Lane, still part of the school today with the recognisable 'Tower' can be seen in this photograph with its surrounding gardens.
1932
Over 90 Years of History
Tower House has been an all-boys, Independent Prep School for over 90 years, with just three boys being enrolled in its first year of opening. Our first Head was George Frederick Edwards B.A. (Hons). Music continued to be taught at the school, along with the other academic subjects such as maths, English, Latin and science.
1935
The Blue Striped Blazer
Tower House School grew quickly over the coming years. The iconic blue striped blazer still used today was introduced as part of the school uniform in the mid-1930s. Even 90 years ago the blazer included the embroidered Tower motif which remains unchanged on the blazers today.
1937
Day Pupils & Boarding School
By 1937, there were 53 day pupils and four boarders aged 8 – 13 who slept in a dormitory at the top of the main Tower House building. The teaching part of the school consisted of three classrooms, a large assembly room and three music rooms.

Headmaster's Welcome
About Tower House
Headmaster's Welcome
Headmaster's Welcome
Learning is life's greatest adventure and at Tower House School we want every boy to arrive each day with a sense of joy, excitement and wonder at what lies ahead.
School should be fun and our innovative and creative curriculum, relaxed and happy ethos and excellent teachers offer just that, in and beyond the classroom. We want our boys to find what they love and to feel inspired to explore those areas with open hearts and minds. This can happen because of our strong commitment to each individual and the school's uniquely supportive environment, in which all boys feel valued and able to contribute on a daily basis.
We value kindness and service to others, which we see every day in the warm relationships between our staff and children and between the boys themselves. We seek to develop young men with a sense of gratitude, an understanding of responsibility and a deep and genuine care for others.
When asked what they most love about Tower House School, the boys are quick to talk about their teachers and for good reason. We are fortunate to have such a professional, committed and caring staff who share their sense of fun and joy with the boys as they strive to support each child in an individual way.
Wherever the boys go next, we want them to face their futures full of confidence and good heart, with dozens of adventures under their belts, with great friends, well-informed minds and with the intellectual curiosity and resilience not only to take on the challenges ahead of them but to actively seek them out.
We hope this website gives a flavour of life at Tower House School but there is no substitute for a visit in person to feel for yourselves what makes this such a magical and special place to come to school. Fun and joy abound. You will be struck by the abundance of smiling faces!
Mr Neill Lunnon, BSc, PGCE
If you would like to find out more about how we achieve our aims and live by our values and commitment to each boy, please visit these pages.

Enrichment Programme
About Tower House
How We Achieve our Aims
Enrichment Programme
Enrichment Programme
Identifying individual passions is a key aspect to helping a child find fulfilment and gain confidence.
This ethos is at the core of a Tower House education. We aim for every boy to feel valued and able to contribute positively to the life of the school. In parallel with this, ensuring that we equip every child with flexible, transferable skills to take on whatever challenges they face in life is vital. If learning these skills through a diverse extracurricular programme is fun and inspiring at the same time, even better!
All boys from Years 1 - 8 are enroled in The Tower House Enrichment Program. This includes:
A varied calendar of school day trips, making the most of what a capital city has to offer, as well as annual residential trips for each year group in the Senior School.
National academic competitions such as the Townsend-Warner History Prize, the Royal Geographical Society Young Geographer of the Year and Maths Olympiads allow the boys to test their knowledge and understanding of their favourite subjects.
Our exceptional and broad offering of extracurricular clubs means there is something new for every pupil to discover! To find out more, please click on the booklet image.
We are delighted that Tower House has received the Eco-School's Green Flag Award.
The Eco-Schools Team was impressed with the whole-school engagement and the clarity of their Eco Code and stated, “The Tower House School’s Eco-Code is a masterpiece. It is easy to understand, not lacking in detail, and yet clear in its objectives.”
Well done to our Eco Committee!

Our Values & Commitment
About Tower House
Our Values & Commitment
Our Values & Commitment
What does it mean to be a Tower House Boy?
Our commitment is to nurture academic excellence within a happy, stimulating and rich learning environment.
School Values
Our School Values are intrinsically linked, able to be put into action individually but also collectively, with every day at Tower House including an array of experiences to foster all our core values. However, at Tower House we also focus one of our six values each half term, to allow a deep dive into how that value can be best lived by our boys in and out of school.
In the Autumn Term, we start with the value which sits at the heart of all we do at Tower House: Kindness, before focusing on Respect in the second half of the term. An opportunity to encourage our boys to listen actively, value diverse perspectives and treat everyone in the school community with kindness and courtesy. There is an emphasis on Courage and Resilience in the Spring Term, as the boys consider what is truly meant to show courage, including moral, physical and social aspects, as well as providing an array of experiences for them to show resilience in the face of challenge. The Summer Term looks at opportunities to show Generosity to others, in terms of generosity of spirit as much as giving generously to others. And finally, we round off the school year with Curiosity, highlighting the wonder and joy behind learning and exploring areas for personal growth.
Through school assemblies, classroom discussions and role-modelling by our older boys in Years 7 and 8, our pupils learn that our values are shown not only through their words but also through their actions.
Our Values are not what we do but who we are at Tower House and act as the foundation on which we build all our boy’s individual and collectively experiences at school.

How We Achieve our Aims
About Tower House
How We Achieve our Aims
How We Achieve our Aims
To ensure we reach our aims and meet our commitments to our pupils and their families we have the following in place:
Opportunities for every boy
We are unapologetically a small school which allows us to work with each boy to identify strengths and support areas that need focus. Pinpointing individual opportunities that will help a boy develop is central to our provision – whether this is to support the academic, social, physical or mental aspects to a boy’s character. Every boy at Tower House will have the chance to take part in:
Tower House Enrichment Program
Regular sports fixtures against local opposition
Junior and Senior School music competitions
Regular musical recitals
A range of trips and residential visits
Highly skilled and subject specialised staff
Our staff are passionate about their field of teaching and are dedicated to sharing their passion for their subject with our boys. As well as inspiring academic curiosity, our boys are guided through the ‘soft skills’ of confidence, empathy and resilience resulting in young men that are well prepared for the demands of senior school and beyond.
Limited class sizes
Our one form entry and limited class sizes results in no child being left behind in or out of a Tower House classroom, with every boy carefully supported to thrive and achieve their full potential. The close, warm and friendly environment means everyone knows each other throughout the school and we are totally committed to fostering support and friendships between pupils within classes and between year groups.
Outstanding facilities for Science, IT, Art, Music, Drama and Sport
Whether it is our award-winning performing arts programme, the state-of-the-art facilities for science, IT and art or our magical reading and resource school library there is place for everyone to get inspired at THS.
Fully inclusive sports programme
We are passionate about supporting our boys in their sporting ambitions! Our fantastic facilities within school and at the local Wimbledon Qualifying and Community Sports Centre enables us to ensure that sport is a core feature on the school timetable.
Everyone is encouraged to take part in competitive matches at home or even abroad during the biennial THS Cricket Tour to Barbados. Our boys compete in several regional and national sporting competitions to pit their skills against the very best sportsmen across the UK.

Broadening Horizons Initiative
About Tower House
How We Achieve our Aims
Broadening Horizons Initiative
Broadening Horizons Initiative
We believe strongly in boys benefitting from two more years with us at Tower House. As they enter Year 7, our boys are encouraged to broaden their horizons and develop new skills and areas of expertise!
This programme aims to stretch pupils in Years 7 & 8 beyond the ISEB Common Entrance syllabus and provides opportunities for them to learn and develop practical skills that prepare them for life beyond the Senior School at THS. It is a time to stretch and challenge the boys in a familiar and supportive environment.
The Tower Project
A highlight for the boys as they enter Year 7, this one-year team-based project challenges boys to develop their entrepreneurial skills in setting up and running a small business. Sponsored by Tenent Financial Education and guided by parent mentors from the world of business, boys are challenged to demonstrate effective communication, critical thinking, problem solving, technological literacy, global awareness, charitable involvement and leadership. External speakers will support them in a range of activities such as website design, effective marketing, financial budgeting and impactful presentation and communication.
Tower House is delighted that this project is sponsored by Tenent Financial Education, who provide financial education for young people. The team at Tenent have worked with THS for several years teaching financial literacy to our Senior School classes.
Applying their ideas and practical knowledge to ‘real world’ situations aims to teach boys vital skills for life: working in a team, the value of careful research and financial management, and how marketing and presentation skills can determine the success of a business.
The final business plans and presentations are judged by our panel of school governors.
The Governors' Project
Introduced in 2024, our Year 7 & 8 boys undertake a summer holiday project of their choice. The range and quality of projects was exceptional, from a detailed European political party manifesto, to pyrography, from designing and creating a fly-fishing rod to documenting a summer of environmental activities. Best of all, each boy presents their project to the full parent body in an evening exhibition to get the new academic year off with a bang!
Leadership
Developing confident and kind individuals who feel ready to have a positive impact on the world around them is a key part of the Tower House ethos. Leadership skills built through hard work, patience and collaboration are nurtured throughout the school but with particular focus in Years 8, whether it is within the classroom, school hall or on the sports field.
To support this vision, our leadership and mentorship scheme gives every Year 8 pupil the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to school life. These roles are designed to develop responsibility, communication, and problem-solving skills while also supporting younger boys in both academic challenges and personal development. Examples of these roles include:
We are immensely proud that our Year 8 pupils lead by example, demonstrating empathy and service that positively influences the whole Tower House community.
Head boy
School Prefect
Head of House
Poet Laureate
Charity Ambassador
Drama Mentor
Junior ThED Talks
Our ThED Talk programme invites external speakers to Tower House to challenge the boys beyond the constraints of the classroom. Building upon this, in Years 7 and 8, the boys are given the opportunity to prepare and present their own talks on a topic they are passionate about and of their choosing. Their curiosity is further encouraged by supporting them in identifying and approaching influential speakers they would like to invite to Tower House to add to the programme.
The Biennial Cricket Tour to Barbados
The THS cricket tour is a major highlight in the Tower House school sports calendar and all Year 7 and Year 8 boys are invited to join the tour, irrespective of ability. This memorable trip offers a perfect blend of culture, stunning natural beauty and the deep-rooted Barbadian passion for cricket. In advance of this trip the boys are expected to raise funds to buy cricket kit that is donated to disadvantaged Barbadian children's cricket clubs. This is a key part of the ethos of this trip, as is meeting and socialising with the local players.
Community and Charity Work
Encouraging our older boys to work on various projects in our local community helps develop well-round characters who are aware of the place they hold in society and the importance of taking an active role in the world around them. Generosity of spirt, giving back and serving others is one of our key values at Tower House.
Running sustainability projects, helping the Friends of Tower House at school events, litter picking on the local common or spending time stacking shelves in the Roehampton Community Box foodbank are just a few examples of how our boys learn to serve their community.
Post Common Entrance Exam Program
The lessons are finished, the exams are done and the results are in! To celebrate the final three weeks that our Year 8 boys are with us, the legendary THS post CE programme gets underway. Learning how to fly a helicopter and Piper PA28 Cherokee, a behind the scenes tour of Twickenham, learning and performing a play-in-a-day and careers talks are some of the many highlights before the Year 8 boys leave Tower House for the final time! Of course, they will always remain Tower House boys and hold an open invitation to return to their school whenever they want. We love to see them back!

We hope this website gives a flavour of life at Tower House School but there is no substitute for a visit in person to feel for yourselves what makes this such a magical and special place to come to school. Fun and joy abound. You will be struck by the abundance of smiling faces!
Mr Neill Lunnon, BSc, PGCE
If you would like to find out more about how we achieve our aims and live by our values and commitment to each boy, please visit these pages.

pageCache.text:
School House System
About Tower House
School House System
School House System
During their first week in Reception, a boy might say he is in the ‘red house’ but by the second week he will firmly know he is a ‘Barnes boy’!
The boys have a strong affiliation with their House. As a school, we encourage healthy competition and the house system provides a perfect mechanism for motivating pupils to do their best across a range of activities. House Points can be awarded for effort and attainment with academic work but can also be achieved through sport, music, drama and art as well as kind, supportive and positive behaviour. A Head’s Award for exceptional effort, performance or behaviour secures 5 House Points! All House Points are collated by Form Teachers and documented on Mr Peyton’s clipboard to be announced in the hugely popular House Points Assembly each week, with House Captains and Vice-Captains delivering a stirring speech to rally the troops. House points are also secured through inter-house sports and music events throughout the year.
Perhaps the most intense of rivalries but always great fun and good humoured. The prestigious House Cup is awarded at Speech Day with the winning House enjoying ‘lashings of ice cream’. Boys belong to one of four houses and follow older siblings into the same House.
Barnes, Chiswick, Kew and Putney

pageCache.pageTitle: Wellbeing and Pastoral Care - Tower House Junior School
pageCache.text:
Wellbeing and Pastoral Care
Junior School
Wellbeing and Pastoral Care
Wellbeing and Pastoral Care
There is nothing more important to us at Tower House than the wellbeing and pastoral care of our boys. Our small and caring community mean that every boy, from Reception to Year 8, is nurtured and feels valued. Having small class sizes helps to create close teacher-pupil relationships; boys feel supported and there is always someone to talk to if they need. As a staff, we ensure that any concerns are addressed quickly; this could be during PSHE lessons, on an individual basis or via our non-verbal Worry Boxes and Worry Monsters.
We have a Mental Health and Wellbeing team that meet regularly to discuss various matters and are on hand to support boys who might need some extra emotional support. There will be moments during their time at school where boys may feel under more pressure, such as during exams and our wellbeing programme ensures the support is available at all times. The boys are thoroughly well known as individuals and no boy falls through the net. There is a special bond between the boys and our staff. Staff-parent relationships are invaluable, to ensure that school and home are working together via open and regular communication.
Each term has a themed week based on Mental Health which involve assemblies, lessons, discussions and interactive workshops for the boys. We ensure that every boy understands how important their mental health is and how to be proactive about developing strong mental as well as physical health. These conversations are an ongoing part of our PSHE curriculum.
For those that require extra support, some of our staff are trained as mental health first aiders and we also have a school counsellor who offers individual sessions to our boys in school.
For more information regarding pastoral care at Tower House, please get in touch with our admissions team on 0208 876 3323 or email admissions@thsboys.org.uk.

pageCache.pageTitle: Tower House Senior School Residential & Day Trips
pageCache.text:
Residential & Day Trips
Senior School
Residential & Day Trips
Residential & Day Trips
School trips often form the most memorable experiences for children at school, providing learning in a different setting, breaking from routine and exploring the world around them.
We aim to make the most of living in such a vibrant, diverse and cultural capital city through regular trips throughout the year; including attending a chemistry workshop at the Royal Institute, filming a TV news report on a green screen at SKY studios and enjoying a behind the scenes tour of the Globe theatre!
The real excitement occurs at our annual residential trips:
In addition, we organise a biennial choir tour for boys from Year 5 – 8. The next tour to Paris in July 2027 will be a fantastic opportunity for the boys to gain experience at performing to a wide variety of audiences, including visitors at Disneyland!
For Years 7 and 8 the THS Cricket Tour is a major highlight in the school calendar for staff, boys and parents. All boys in these year groups are invited to join the tour, irrespective of ability and this memorable trip offers a perfect blend of stunning natural beauty and the deep-rooted Barbadian culture and passion for cricket.
In advance of this trip the boys are expected to raise funds to buy cricket kit that is donated to disadvantaged Barbadian children’s cricket clubs. This is a key part of the ethos of this trip, as is meeting and socialising with the local players.

pageCache.pageTitle: Early Years (EYFS) Curriculum Richmond upon Thames
pageCache.text:
EYFS Curriculum
Reception
EYFS Curriculum
EYFS Curriculum
Our Reception days at Tower House are busy, fun and varied! We have plenty of learning to do but the key is to ensure the boys are feeling confident and comfortable, are making good friends and are feeling cared for and fully supported. We want to see as many smiling faces as possible. The boys enjoy a wide range of activities from learning phonics and number bonds through to cooking, swimming, music, PE, ICT and reading time. A weekly highlight for the boys is story-time with the Head and Deputy Head. It is their highlight too! And then, there is the magic of Forest School.
Our all-boy environment allows us to tailor the Reception curriculum and design lessons that exclusively suit the learning styles of boys and ensure that every day they are engaged and stimulated. The boys spend their first year at Tower House familiarising themselves with their daily routines, making friends and gaining confidence. This year, we believe, is all about laying a firm foundation on which to build, allowing the boys to flourish and thrive as they develop into independent and happy learners. Each lesson combines formal teacher-led instruction with time to play and explore, providing the perfect preparation for Key Stage 1.
Reception follows the Early Years Foundation Stage Curriculum, which includes three key areas:
Physical development
Personal, social and emotional development
Communication and language
These three key areas are developed and strengthened through literacy, numeracy, understanding the world and expressive arts and design.

Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care
Wraparound Care
Before School Care (BSC) is available from 07:30 - 08.10 each morning. Boys using this provision should be brought to the main school entrance on Sheen Lane and directed toward the BSC classroom next to the science lab where a member of staff will be on-hand to supervise.
Junior School Late Class takes place from when school finishes until 16.00. It is intended mainly for boys who are waiting for an older sibling in the Senior School but also those waiting to go to After School Care. Supervising staff will bring Late Class attendees to the Junior School exit.
After School Care (ASC) runs from 16:05 until 18:00. Parents can collect their children at any point during After School Care from the ASC classroom.
Both BSC & ASC run on an ad hoc basis. Parents will be charged a fee for this provision which is added termly to the school bill at the end of term. Please note that charges will be for 1 hour if children are picked up by 17:00 and for 2 hours if they are collected between 17:00 and 18:00. An email to book a place should be sent to the school office (secretary@thsboys.org.uk) as much in advance as possible, although boys can be dropped at BSC without prior notice if required.

Future Schools
Leavers' Destinations
Leavers' Destinations
Tower House boys complete their Common Entrance exams in the summer of Year 8. We are incredibly proud of each and every one of them as they move onto a wide range of outstanding Senior Schools.

pageCache.pageTitle: Independent & Private Prep School Admissions Richmond upon Thames
pageCache.text:
Admissions
Admissions
Your Tower House Adventure Starts Here
It is very important to us that our boys flourish and thrive during their time at Tower House and have every chance of emerging as confident, curious and well-rounded young men. Our admissions process has evolved to enable us to learn more about our prospective boys and their families and understand their individual needs and concerns, whilst also allowing parents to meet more members of staff, get to know other families and most importantly for the boys themselves to become familiar with Tower House and make some new friends.
Our families come from a wide range of areas in South-West London, including East Sheen, Mortlake, Barnes, Richmond, Ham, Twickenham, Kew, Chiswick, Putney, Wimbledon and Wandsworth. We have a Tower House bus service that collects our pupils each morning from Richmond, Kew, Mortlake, Putney and Barnes.
How do I arrange a visit to Tower House?
We would be delighted to show you around our lovely school. This can be through a termly Open Event, or a personal tour arranged at your convenience. Please contact our Head of Admissions, Vicky Singlehurst to arrange a visit:
Admissions: 0208 876 3323
Emails: admissions@thsboys.org.uk (please always include your telephone number in the email)
What are the main entry points into Tower House?
The main entry point is into the Reception class. Your son would join this class in the first September after his fourth birthday. In older year groups in the Junior School and Senior School, we offer occasional places to families on our waiting lists as they arise.
If you would like more information, please contact our Head of Admissions, Vicky Singlehurst on 0208 876 3323. Alternatively, you can complete an admissions enquiry form and we will arrange a call to discuss the admissions process in more detail.
How do I register my son for a place at Tower House?
In Reception, the first 18 boys registered are placed on our main list and will be offered a place at Tower House 18 months before the boys are due to start at school. In older year groups, we offer occasional places to families on our waiting lists as they arise.
To register for a place in Reception, as well as inclusion on a year group waiting list, we ask parents to complete an admissions registration form and pay a £120 registration fee.
Are there any assessments as part of the admissions process?
Tower House is non-selective in Reception.
For places in Year 1 and above, before an offer of a place is made, we invite all prospective applicants into the school to spend a morning with us. The applicant will largely spend the time with his future classmates, taking part in the lessons of the day. Depending on the age of the child, a light assessment in English and maths is also likely to take place. We also ask parents to share their son's latest school report with us.
When is your next Open Event?
Our Open Events take place termly. We would be delighted to welcome you to the school to meet staff, current parents and most importantly, our wonderful Year 8 boys who will give you a tour of their school. You will also have a presentation from the Head and have a chance to talk to him and the Deputy Head, should you have any questions.
To find out the date of the next Open Event and register to attend, please visit our Open Events and Tours page.
How are new children helped to integrate into Tower House?
We pride ourselves on enabling boys to settle in quickly. The small nature of the school means that new pupils and their families integrate easily into their classes and the wider community.
Before starting life at Tower House, we have a detailed summer induction programme for new Reception boys. For older pupils in the Junior School and Senior School, we also recommend that your son comes into school for a morning to spend time with their new classmates in the term preceding their start at Tower House.
All staff take the time to make sure that new boys feel part of each class and are supported not only in their learning, but in all areas of school life. Each child is assigned a couple of ‘buddies’ to take care of them during their first few weeks of school and there is regular contact between parents and their son’s Head of Year. We also ensure that parents are quickly integrated into the Tower House community with support from our parent’s association, Friends of Tower House (FOTH).

pageCache.pageTitle: Independent Boys Prep School Admissions Process Richmond upon Thames
pageCache.text:
Admissions Process
Admissions Process
Admissions Process
Start Your Admissions Journey With a Few Simple Steps
Pick up the phone and give us a call, or complete an admissions enquiry form by clicking the button below. We will then be able to provide you with detailed information about Tower House. Please note that once an enquiry form is completed, you will receive your login details for your admissions account. Please do check your junk inbox to ensure you don’t miss out on any emails from us.
Head of Admissions: Vicky Singlehurst
Email: admissions@thsboys.org.uk (please include your telephone number in all communications with us)
Book yourself into an Open Event or personal tour by clicking the button below, so that you can come and get to know Tower House, our staff and pupils better.
An Open Event will give you a chance to meet Neill Lunnon, our Head, as well as current parents. You will be given a tour of the school by two Year 8 boys and will have a chance to ask lots of questions.
A personal tour with Neill Lunnon will give you a chance to have a deeper and more detailed tour of the school. You will have plenty of opportunities to ask questions and get to know Neill and our staff.
Prospective parents often choose to attend an Open Event and then follow this up with a personal tour. We are very happy to accommodate parents with whatever they would prefer.
Complete an admissions registration form to begin your application by clicking the button below. Once completed, if you haven’t already submitted an enquiry you will receive your login details for your admissions account. Please do check your junk inbox to ensure you don’t miss out on any emails from us.
Registering your son does not entitle him to a place at Tower House, as entry above Reception is always following some form of assessment and trial morning.
A non-refundable registration fee of £120 is payable for each student.
Your Child's Journey Begins Here
Choose the stage you are considering for your child and learn more about the process to join our Tower House Family
Reception - Visit Us
We would be delighted to welcome you to one of our Open Events to meet staff, current parents and most importantly our wonderful Year 8 boys who will give you a tour of their school. You will also have a presentation from the Head and have a chance to talk to him and the Deputy Head, should you have any questions. We also offer personal tours of the school by the Head in small groups if the Open Event date is inconvenient for you.
Register
Once you decide that you would like your child to attend Tower House, we ask you to submit the online registration form, with the required registration fee of £120.
Reception - Place Offered
As Tower House is a non-selective school, there is no entrance test to start in Reception. Siblings of children already in the school have a confirmed offer. The first twenty pupils, including siblings, to register in each year are considered as guaranteed places.
Reception - Get Ready to Settle In
For our new Reception boys we know that starting school is an extremely important milestone in every child’s life and can be an anxious time for parents too. With this in mind, we have developed a detailed induction programme in the summer before the boys start, to allow parents to meet more members of staff, get to know other families and most importantly for the boys themselves to become familiar with Tower House and make some new friends. Reception staff also visit each pupil in their home as an opportunity to get to know the families and each boy in an informal and familiar setting. For more information on the induction process and the events organised, please contact the Head of Admissions, Vicky Singlehurst.
Reception - Starting School
Reception boys come in for half a day at Tower House for the first few days of term to help them settle in and this is built up over the first week until the boys remain at school for the whole day. Our staff develop a careful timetable in the first term to ensure that the boys settle in quickly, are happy and excited about coming into school.
Inducting our new THS families
The Tower House families are right at the heart of the Tower House community and we are proud that lifelong friendships are made at our school events and functions. The Friends of Tower House (FOTH) provides a wonderful network of supportive parents that are happy to answer questions and provide assistance to new families. The school introduces new families to FOTH as soon as is convenient to new parents.
Reception School Day in the Life
08:30AM
Reception Registration
The Reception teacher welcomes the boys into school and helps them prepare for the day ahead. The children complete ‘morning challenges’, sing songs together and complete the register.
08:40AM
Assembly
The school comes together twice a week to celebrate achievements and recognise hard work. Topics and themes such as local charities and mental health awareness are often discussed. The Junior School will join together with the Senior School once a week.
09:10AM
Reception - Lessons begin
The children have daily phonics sessions where they learn the skills involved in learning to read and write. The boys then work their way through a ‘carousel’ of activities aimed at supporting and developing their skills across the Early Years Foundation Stage.
09.40AM
Reception - Breaktime
The Reception children mix with the Year One boys in the playground.
10.00AM
Specialist teachers
The children attend lessons run by specialist teachers, from music and a trip to the school library, through to a session in the IT suite, a games session or the weekly trip to Forest School; they thoroughly enjoy the breath and width of the curriculum.
11:45AM
Reception - Lunch
Lunch at Tower House is a very social and lively time. The catering team designs a varied and healthy weekly menu with regular themed lunches such as Thai, Mexican or French food days. Where possible ingredients are sourced locally and seasonally to create fresher, healthier and environmentally friendly lunches. Playtime is with the Year 1 boys.
01:00PM
Reception - Afternoon register
Afternoon register is always followed by daily maths sessions.
02:00PM
Time to think independently
The children have ‘thinking for themselves’ time, this is an opportunity to ‘self-select’ from enhanced continuous provision in the classroom.
03:00PM
Story Time
The children sit on the carpet and are read a story by their class teacher.
Junior School - Visit Us
We would be delighted to welcome you to one of our Open Events to meet staff, current parents and most importantly our wonderful Year 8 boys who will give you a tour of their school. You will also have a presentation from the Head and have a chance to talk to him and the Deputy Head, should you have any questions. We also offer personal tours of the school by the Head in small groups if the Open Event date is inconvenient for you.
Register
Once you decide that you would like your child to attend Tower House, we ask you to submit the online registration form, with the required registration fee of £120.
Junior School - Finding Out More
For entry into Year 1 or 2 we invite the prospective pupil to join their future class for an hour or so to assess their suitability and ensure he would be happy and content in this educational environment. Boys wishing to enter Year 3 and above are invited into the school to undertake online assessments in English and Maths. During this time the prospective pupil is able to meet some of the staff, spend some time in the school (often with their future class) and take part in an informal interview with the Head or Deputy Head, during which they may get an opportunity to read aloud. The purpose of the informal interview is not to test what the boy has learned, but to learn more about him, what he enjoys and what he may bring to the life of the school. We aim to assess whether we feel he will be able to cope with the educational challenges at the school. It is very important to us that the boys flourish and thrive during their time at Tower House and have every chance of emerging confident, curious and well-rounded young men. As a result of this informal interview the school reserves the right to postpone or refuse admission to a boy if it be considered necessary.
Junior School - Place Offered
Following a successful visit to Tower House, a formal offer of a place will be made and settling in sessions will be scheduled. Offers are made in order of registration and siblings of Prep School pupils are given priority.
Settling In
We invite the boys into school for a morning in the summer term or the term preceding their start. This provides an excellent introduction for each new boy, in order to make some new friends and help dispel any nerves before they start with us.
Inducting our new THS families
The Tower House families are right at the heart of the Tower House community and we are proud that lifelong friendships are made at our school events and functions. The Friends of Tower House (FOTH) provides a wonderful network of supportive parents that are happy to answer questions and provide assistance to new families. The school introduces new families to FOTH as soon as is convenient to new parents.
Junior School Day in the Life
08:25AM
Registration
Each day starts in their form rooms with a smile and welcome from their form teacher. The register is taken as the boys prepare for the day ahead in order to hit the ground running. It also gives time for some quiet reading, drawing or discussions about topics of interest.
08:40AM
Assembly
The school comes together twice a week to celebrate achievements and recognise hard work. A whole school assembly combines with a Junior School one to cover topics and themes such as local charities and mental health awareness. The Junior School boys love joining the older ones.
09:10AM
Lessons begin
It’s time for some serious learning! Morning lessons are dominated by maths and English but could involve subjects from across the curriculum. The Head either reads to or hears the boys read to him every week, which is a real highlight for him, and us!
10.00AM
Breaktime
Time to interact and have fun together as the boys head into the playground for break and the chance to mix across year groups. There is so much to choose from as the boys let off from energy through fun games and activities. The ’Octoplay’ shapes are always a firm favourite.
10:20AM
Learning continues
It’s back to class and time to further develop their numeracy and literacy or perhaps deal with some well-being issues in PSHE. The laptops may be out, enhancing the boy’s learning experience. There is lots of collaborative work as boys are set challenging task in pairs or small groups.
12:00PM
Lunch
Lunch at Tower House is a very social and lively time. The catering team designs a varied and healthy weekly menu with regular themed lunches such as Thai, Mexican or French food days. Ingredients are sourced locally and seasonally to create fresher, healthier and environmentally friendly lunches. The boys enjoy the food at THS. After refuelling, there’s more time in the playground.
01:00PM
Afternoon lessons
The array of lessons continues as the boys enjoy time in the science lab, in drama, art, music or PE, or working on their coding in the ICT suite. There are House Points or Head’s Awards to be earned for hard work and attainment in the classroom.
02:00PM
Games sessions
Sport is important at Tower House, taught from the earliest years by our specialist sports teachers. Boys are encouraged to develop their agility, skills and stamina through a variety of team games.
03:30PM
After school clubs
The school day is over but there is plenty of fun still on the cards as the boys head into the Clubs Programme. We are proud to offer a wide variety of extra-curricular activities, from pottery, coding, fencing, karate, arts & crafts and much more. There is something for everyone and opportunities for all.
Senior School - Visit Us
We would be delighted to welcome you to one of our Open Events to meet staff, current parents and most importantly our wonderful Year 8 boys who will give you a tour of their school. You will also have a presentation from the Head and have a chance to talk to him and the Deputy Head, should you have any questions. We also offer tours of the school by the Head in small groups if the Open Event date is inconvenient for you.

During this time the prospective pupil is able to meet some of the staff, spend some time in the school (often with their future class) and take part in an informal interview with the Head or Deputy Head, during which they may get an opportunity to read aloud. The purpose of the informal interview is not to test what the boy has learned, but to learn more about him, what he enjoys and what he may bring to the life of the school. We aim to assess whether we feel he will be able to cope with the educational challenges at the school. It is very important to us that the boys flourish and thrive during their time at Tower House and have every chance of emerging confident, curious and well-rounded young men. As a result of this informal interview the school reserves the right to postpone or refuse admission to a boy if it be considered necessary.

Following a successful visit and assessment at Tower House, a formal offer of a place will be made and settling in sessions will be scheduled. Offers are made in order of registration and siblings of Prep School pupils are given priority.
Settling In
We invite the boys int
